title: Capacity Snapshot Cockpit — Dedicated GPU Fleet Controls & Burst Playbook
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, glanceable cockpit for Dedicated GPU fleets that surfaces real-time health, suggested autoscale/burst actions, and a lightweight playbook users can invoke during incidents. This ticket covers the initial hi-fi screens, interaction states for manual/automatic burst toggles, a condensed cost-latency tradeoff widget, and a contextual playbook drawer with experiment/runbook links.
acceptance_criteria: Hi-fi Figma screens for cockpit (desktop + tablet) delivered with responsive variants
Interactive prototype (Figma/Framer) demonstrating: manual burst toggle, autoscale policy quick-edit, and playbook invocation
Accessibility pass: color contrast, keyboard focus states, and descriptive aria labels documented
Design handoff package in Drive with token list, component specs, and UX rationale
UX review feedback addressed and sign-off from PM (Marco Chen) and Eng lead (Riley Thompson)
decisions: Prioritize a compact single-row summary for fleets with the ability to expand to a 3-column detail view on hover/click.
Expose a simple autoscale quick-edit (min/max/target latency) inline to reduce context switching; advanced policy editor remains in Console Advanced tab.
Burst mode is surfaced as a two-state action (Immediate Burst / Scheduled Burst) with an estimated cost delta shown pre-confirmation.
Cost-latency tradeoff visualization uses an embedded sparkline + cost delta microcard rather than a heavy chart to keep the cockpit dense.
Playbook content is curated links + short runbook steps in a right-side drawer (max 5 steps) to keep the primary surface focused on telemetry and controls.
tradeoffs: Density vs. discoverability: compact view reduces screen real-estate but hides deeper telem — mitigated by hover-to-expand and drill-in flows.
Simplified autoscale controls lower cognitive load but will not cover complex rate-limiting use cases — advanced config remains in dedicated policy screens.
Estimating cost deltas client-side increases responsiveness but risks small inaccuracies; add a server-verified calc on confirm.
reviews: 2026-03-05: PM review (Marco Chen) — asked for clearer failure-state guidance and an explicit fallback when bursts fail to provision.
2026-03-08: Eng design review (Riley Thompson) — flagged KV cache metrics are not currently exposed via telemetry pipeline; proposed placeholder state and an ENG follow-up (ENG-19876).
2026-03-12: Accessibility review (Jin Park) — recommended increased contrast for the microcard cost delta and keyboard shortcuts for toggles; updated mocks applied.
next_steps: Resolve ENG dependency to surface KV cache hit/miss metrics (ENG-19876) before final handoff
Create short usability test script and recruit 6 internal SRE/Platform engineers for moderated sessions (target week of 2026-03-22)
Produce handoff tokens and CSS variables in the Drive handoff folder
Coordinate with Console PM to schedule a canary rollout for Dedicated clusters after implementation
